label: Late original-phase steps (t>=4) and <DEL> in sequences that start with n
explanation: Fires only in sequences whose first original token is n (97.5% of activation mass). It fires from about step 4 through the <DEL> step (t <= L) and is silent at steps 0-2 and during the whole copy phase. The current input token barely matters. Magnitude grows over the first few active steps (about 0.5 of max at t=4 rising to about 1.0 at t=6-7) and is largest when the sequence starts n n. It drops a little at <DEL>, where it is effectively a signal that the first output will be n. Weak residual activations (3.6% of mass) occur when n is the second token rather than the first, and at t=3. It rarely stays off on a matching step; the few cases are sequences with repeated n.

issues: Recall by count is only 0.82, but the 12.5k missed test steps carry just 3.4% of the activation mass. They are almost all tiny activations (0.00-0.08 of max) in sequences where n is the second token, plus some at t=3. This is a weak tail, not a systematic missed class worth covering. Extending the predicate to t>=3 drops F1 to 0.833 (precision 0.81). Adding orig(1)==n drops F1 to 0.714 (precision 0.58). Restricting to orig(1)==n with first_tok!=n gives precision 0.11 and mass 2.3%.
The 243 false positives are mostly 'n ? n ...' sequences with a repeated n, where the feature stays off at t=4 and starts at t=5. This matches what the explanation says and is small.

All factual claims check out on the dev profile and test scores. There are zero activations at t=0-2 and in the copy phase. At t==4 the feature's coverage is concentrated in the lower-middle activation quartiles, while t>=6 is concentrated in the top quartile (0.45), so magnitude rises across the active steps as claimed. The 'n n' starts are enriched in the top quartile (0.076 vs 0.002 in the bottom). The <DEL> step is spread fairly evenly across the middle and top quartiles, consistent with a modest drop there.
